newsitem.title: MEXICO: Drug lords seen behind Mexico police slaying.
newsitem.headline: Drug lords seen behind Mexico police slaying.

text.p: Mexican authorities said on Monday they believed drug traffickers were behind the murder of an antinarcotics agent found dead with his three bodyguards in Mexico City this past weekend.

The body of Jorge Garcia Vargas, a commander of the National Antinarcotics Institute based in the northern border city of Tijuana, was found late on Saturday in a car in a northern Mexico City suburb.
He and his guards, who were not identified until Sunday, had been strangled to death and may have been tortured, officials said.
"There were marks, possibly of torture ... their hands were bound and one of them still had a rope round his neck," police official Angel Diaz Ortiz said.
Another police official added: "This has to be related to drug trafficking because of the way it was carried out."
Radio station Radio Red reported that authorities suspected the Arellano Felix brothers, who head the Tijuana drugs cartel based in Baja California state, of ordering the killings.
Garcia had been investigating money laundering involving prominent businessmen in Baja, radio and TV reports said.

The brothers Ramon, Javier and Benjamin Arellano Felix are also sought by authorities for their alleged role in the 1993 murder of Cardinal Juan Jesus Posadas Ocampo, the Roman Catholic archbishop of Guadalajara.
